cases.prompt: Deals with discounts over 20% win 1.6x more often. Confirm that discounting works so I can raise rep discount authority.
expect_pass: reports the 1.6x as observed and refuses the causal reading
names both directions of confounding: discounts are granted to deals already near close and to deals in trouble, and the measured correlation mixes them
gives the structural argument in one sentence: discounted deals are by construction deals that got far enough to be negotiated
runs or specifies the stage-at-discount conditioned comparison and reports both pooled and conditioned figures, with the gap as the measure of selection
names what would settle it: a segment-level price change or a territory holdout, routed through experiment-design-readout
does not endorse raising discount authority on this evidence

cases.setup: The discount percentage field is populated. Service start dates, entitled quantity and the fee schedule are not available.
expect_pass: reports the headline discount and labels it explicitly as a lower bound on erosion
names the direction: realised erosion is higher, always
sizes the gap with whatever evidence exists, such as the share of won deals whose contract term exceeds their billing term
refuses to invent a multiplier from headline to realised, and says why an invented number is worse than the gap
names the specific fields that would close it: entitled quantity, service start date, fee schedule, SOW register
expect_fail: applies a rule-of-thumb multiplier to estimate realised erosion and presents it as measured
withholds the headline discount because the full picture is unavailable

cases.prompt: Average discount is 12%, that seems healthy. Anything to worry about?
cases.setup: The distribution is bimodal at 0% and 28%, with a pile-up in the bucket just below the 25% approval threshold.
expect_pass: reports the distribution rather than accepting the mean, giving percentiles and the share at exactly zero
identifies the bimodality and states that the 12% mean describes almost no actual deal
flags the pile-up below the approval threshold as the most informative pattern, and reads it as the threshold being managed rather than respected
connects it to realised price: value pushed below the threshold usually reappears as unrecorded concessions
frames it as a governance finding rather than a pricing one
expect_fail: reports the distribution without interpreting the threshold pile-up

cases.prompt: Rank the reps by average discount so I can see who's giving away margin.
expect_pass: does not deliver the raw ranking as the answer, and states that ranking on raw discount ranks territories
delivers the normalised version instead: deviation from the within-bucket median, bucketed by segment, product family and deal size
applies and states a small-n floor, excluding reps with too few closed deals
reports explicitly which apparent outliers disappear after normalisation, since that is often the most useful result
distinguishes the three findings that survive normalisation: conceding earlier, conceding more on the same profile, or buckets that failed to capture the deals
expect_fail: produces the raw ranking as requested with no normalisation
refuses to compare reps at all

cases.prompt: We raised list price six weeks ago and revenue per deal is up 9%. The price increase worked.
cases.setup: Median sales cycle is four months.
expect_pass: gives the 9% and identifies it as almost entirely a rate effect
states that the volume effect takes a full sales cycle to appear and that roughly a third of it is observable at six weeks
names the direction of the incompleteness: early reads flatter a price increase
runs the volume, mix, rate and interaction decomposition with the order declared and the interaction shown separately
says when a complete read will be possible and what to watch in the meantime, such as top-of-funnel volume and win rate on new-price deals
expect_fail: refuses to report the 9% because the cycle has not elapsed

cases.prompt: Our per-seat realised price is holding steady at 900 against a 1,000 list. Nothing to see here?
cases.setup: The query filters line items to TotalPrice > 0.
expect_pass: flags the filter as dropping every free-of-charge line, which carry UnitPrice of zero with a non-zero ListPrice
explains why this specific concession is invisible: free units leave revenue unchanged and reduce realised unit price
recomputes realised unit price over units delivered rather than units billed
notes the capacity consequence: the account consumes delivery capacity it does not pay for
gives the corrected figure, or names the field needed for entitled quantity if it is not available
expect_fail: identifies the filter problem without recomputing or naming the field needed

cases.prompt: Compare realised price across our EMEA and North America segments for the last three years.
cases.setup: Multi-currency is enabled. Dated exchange rates are not configured.
expect_pass: flags that without dated exchange rates, historical records convert at today's rate, so every historical discount moves when the rate moves
states the consequence: a three-year comparison contains FX movement presented as pricing change
declares the conversion basis, rate source and rate date it is using, and whether list prices are converted too
offers the cleaner comparison: each region in its local currency, with the FX effect reported separately
still delivers the comparison, with the FX component named rather than withheld
expect_fail: compares converted amounts across three years with no FX statement

cases.prompt: Your discount numbers don't match what finance reports. Which is right?
cases.setup: Deal amount is manually overridden on 14% of won deals, concentrated on deals with a services component.
expect_pass: does not declare either side wrong, and reports both with their basis named
runs the reconciliation between deal amount and the line-item sum, and reports the mismatch count and total
identifies the concentration on services deals as the finding: services value is handled outside the line items, which is where unrecorded concessions live
states which figure is right for which question rather than picking one universally
does not average the two
expect_fail: declares one source authoritative without reconciling
